brief: JPMorgan US Market Intelligence moves to a Tactically Cautious / Neutral stance. The chain: Warsh's post-Jackson Hole view that the US is at full employment with inflation too high makes the Sep 16 meeting live, so CPI on Sep 11 outranks Friday's NFP, and NFP inverts into a good-news-is-bad-news setup because a stronger print lifts yields and weighs on equities. Four further inputs stack on. Positioning gives no clean directional read, post-Labor Day issuance widens credit spreads, September screens as the worst SPX month before a strong Q4, and Momentum is down more than 21% (JPMPURE) and nearly 34% (JPPQMO) from June highs, outside typical 10-15% drawdowns. Fundamentals are held intact: recession is unlikely, earnings should print strongly for two more quarters, and two 25bp hikes would not derail the bull market. The conclusion is chop rather than a dramatic pullback, arguing for reduced net longs and a dollar-neutral approach. The monetization menu is +NDX vs. -RTY, Mag7 over AI/Memory/Semis, short credit ETFs and long VIX as hedges. The note also carries Feroli's NFP preview, an AVGO earnings preview, weekly delta-one flows, consumer spending and credit default updates.
